chapter: Early years and the Sonny South
title: Sonny South Syncopators personnel, 1928
summary: He joined the ten- or eleven-piece reading band in 1928 and names its members: Leo Dejan, Gilly, Lee, Emile Fritz and others.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Up until 1939 I just played music for a living. I see. Well, you know, like I played with the Sonny South Syncopated, I was an organized band. Most of my job was mostly with ten piece artists, you know, large bands. And I worked with them for quite a while. I started with the Sonny South Syncopated in 1928.

Reading band, yeah. We had ten pieces, eleven pieces with the piano. Who was he meant to? We had Lee, a fellow by the name of Lee, playing voice alto, I mean third alto, Emile Fritz tenor, Elliot Taylor, voice sax, Richard McNein, guitar, a fellow by the name of Charles, bass, Sently J, trumpet. Who? Sently J, Anthony Sently J.
Yeah, I never did know him.
No, you didn't know him. You got out the picture.
Leo Dejom, I don't know if you know him.

Who I heard of the trumpet player. The trumpet player, Leo Dejom. That's Harold's brother. Yeah, and the drummer was a fellow by the name of Gilly. I don't know if you know him. That's the original Sonny South band. Gilly, songs about Dejom and myself on piano. You sang, huh? You were a singer, huh? No, Dejom was a song. Oh, you didn't sing at all.
I played. I played. I played.
I played. I played. I played. Well, Leo was a singer? No, Leo Dejom, yeah.
He was a singer. Yeah, I see.
Did that band play mostly over here and there? All over. Well, he played on the other side, too, huh? Yeah, we played on the other side.
